page_title: Gathering Intel on Intel AVX-512 Transitions

sources.entry: Gathering Intel on Intel AVX-512 Transitions - Measures what the vendor leaves untimed in an AVX-512 licence change, a throttled phase then a frequency step.

summary.title: Gathering Intel on Intel AVX-512 Transitions
summary.one_liner: Wide AVX/AVX-512 instructions on Intel SKX-era CPUs trigger a voltage-only throttling phase (about 4x slower dispatch, roughly 8-20 μs) and sometimes a frequency change with a halt, measured with microbenchmarks.
keywords: avx license levels l0 l1 l2
takeaways: After about 680 μs without using AVX upper bits, the first wide instruction triggers a voltage transition during which dispatch runs about 4x slower.
The throttling is fine-grained and applies only while wide instructions are in flight; nearby scalar adds are also slowed, but spaced-out ones run at full speed.
On the tested W-2104-class SKX chip, 512-bit instructions drop the frequency from 3.2 GHz (L0) to 2.8 GHz (L1), with an ~11 μs halt and a ~650 μs low-frequency period.
Light 256-bit instructions show the same voltage-only slowdown but no frequency change, and 128-bit instructions show no effect.
summary.summary: The author builds a microbenchmark framework (freq-bench) that runs a payload at periodic duty cycles while sampling frequency and IPC at 1 μs intervals, then uses it to examine AVX-512 and AVX transitions on a W-series Skylake-SP CPU. Tests with 256-bit and 512-bit vpor and vpord, mixed with scalar add instructions, reveal a ~9-10 μs voltage-only throttle with about 4x slowdown, followed for 512-bit by a halt and frequency step from L0 to L1. Voltage readings from MSR_PERF_STATUS on a mobile i7-6700HQ are used to support the idea that throttling waits for a voltage increase. The post also tests attenuation and lists untested areas such as heavy instructions and frequency dependence.
